framework.name: EU Cyber Resilience Act
framework.description: EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation 2024/2847) — mandatory cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements. In force October 2024; manufacturers must comply by October 2027.

objects.title: Manufacturer Obligations
objects.description: Conformity assessment, CE marking, market surveillance cooperation, and EU registration requirements.

objects.title: Security by Design Requirements
objects.description: Essential cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements (Annex I, Part I).

objects.title: Vulnerability Handling
objects.description: Vulnerability identification, coordinated disclosure, security updates, ENISA notification, and SBOM requirements.

objects.title: Documentation & Transparency
objects.description: Technical documentation, user instructions, and EU declaration of conformity requirements.

objects.title: Market Operators
objects.description: Obligations for importers and distributors placing products with digital elements on the EU market.

objects.title: Support & Lifecycle
objects.description: Support period definition and end-of-life communication requirements.

objects.title: Conformity Assessment
objects.description: Products with digital elements undergo the appropriate conformity assessment procedure before being placed on the market (Art. 32).

objects.title: CE Marking
objects.description: Products that comply with essential requirements bear the CE marking and an EU declaration of conformity is drawn up (Art. 28).

objects.title: Market Surveillance Cooperation
objects.description: Manufacturers cooperate with market surveillance authorities and provide all necessary information upon request (Art. 33).

objects.title: Registration in EUDAMED
objects.description: Products in important/critical classes are registered in the European database (Art. 27).

objects.title: No Known Exploitable Vulnerabilities
objects.description: Products are placed on the market without known exploitable vulnerabilities in the product components (Annex I, Part I, §1).

objects.title: Secure Default Configuration
objects.description: Products are delivered with a secure-by-default configuration, including the ability to reset to factory settings (Annex I, Part I, §2).

objects.title: Access Control
objects.description: Products protect against unauthorised access through appropriate access control mechanisms including authentication and identity management (Annex I, Part I, §3).

objects.title: Data Confidentiality
objects.description: Products protect the confidentiality of stored, transmitted, or otherwise processed data using state-of-the-art cryptography (Annex I, Part I, §4).

objects.title: Data Integrity
objects.description: Products protect the integrity of commands, programs, data, and configurations against unauthorised manipulation (Annex I, Part I, §5).

objects.title: Data Minimisation
objects.description: Products process only data that is necessary for their intended purpose (Annex I, Part I, §6).

objects.title: Availability Protection
objects.description: Products protect the availability of essential functions including resilience against and mitigation of denial-of-service attacks (Annex I, Part I, §7).

objects.title: Minimal Attack Surface
objects.description: Products are designed to minimise their attack surface including external interfaces (Annex I, Part I, §8).

objects.title: Incident Impact Limitation
objects.description: Products are designed to limit the impact of an incident on other products or networks (Annex I, Part I, §9).

objects.title: Security Monitoring
objects.description: Products provide security-related information through logging and monitoring capabilities (Annex I, Part I, §10).

objects.title: Vulnerability Identification
objects.description: Vulnerabilities in the product and its third-party components are identified and documented including a software bill of materials (SBOM) (Annex I, Part II, §1).

objects.title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure
objects.description: A coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy is published and maintained (Annex I, Part II, §5).

objects.title: Timely Security Updates
objects.description: Security updates addressing vulnerabilities are made available without undue delay; the update period extends for the expected product lifetime (Annex I, Part II, §4).

objects.title: ENISA Notification
objects.description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents are reported to ENISA within 24 hours of discovery (Art. 14).

objects.title: SBOM Availability
objects.description: A software bill of materials is maintained in a machine-readable format and provided to market surveillance authorities upon request (Annex I, Part II, §1).

objects.title: Technical Documentation
objects.description: Technical documentation is drawn up before the product is placed on the market and kept up to date throughout the product lifetime (Art. 31).

objects.title: Instructions to Users
objects.description: Clear and comprehensive instructions are provided in the language(s) required by the member state(s), covering secure installation, operation, and update procedures (Annex II).

objects.title: EU Declaration of Conformity
objects.description: An EU declaration of conformity is drawn up and kept up to date for 10 years after market placement (Art. 28).

objects.title: Importer Obligations
objects.description: Importers verify that manufacturers have performed the conformity assessment and that technical documentation and CE marking are in order before placing products on the EU market (Art. 19).

objects.title: Distributor Obligations
objects.description: Distributors verify CE marking and accompanying documents and act to address non-conformity before making products available on the market (Art. 20).

objects.title: Support Period Definition
objects.description: The expected support period is specified and at minimum five years unless the intended product lifetime is shorter (Art. 13(8)).

objects.title: End-of-Life Communication
objects.description: End-of-support is communicated to users in advance; options for continued security coverage are provided where possible (Art. 13(10)).
